How a sourdough loaf rises without commercial yeast, and where its sour taste comes from.

## Two jobs, two microbes

The wild yeasts in a [[sourdough-starter]] ferment sugars from the flour into carbon dioxide, which inflates the dough. The lactic acid bacteria make little gas; they make the lactic and acetic acid that give the bread its sourness and help it keep.

## The gas needs somewhere to go

The carbon dioxide only becomes rise because the [[gluten-network]] traps it in small bubbles. A dough with weak gluten lets the same gas escape.

## Slow is normal

A sourdough rise often takes 4 to 12 hours at room temperature, against 1 to 2 hours for baker's yeast, because the wild yeast population is smaller and the acid slows it down.

## What I said reading it

Sour and rise come from different organisms, so a baker can push one without the other.
